offers_products.reason: Journal Technologies sells case management software licences and SaaS to courts. The company also publishes subscription legal newspapers.

offers_services.reason: Journal Technologies does implementation, consulting, and ongoing support and maintenance for court and agency software systems.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Software goes to courts and agencies. Newspaper subscribers are mostly attorneys and legal professionals buying for work.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Courts, government agencies, and law firms buy its case management software and legal publications.

recurring_revenue.reason: Software maintenance, hosted subscriptions, and newspaper subscriptions bring repeat revenue from the same customers.

cyclical_demand.reason: Courts and agencies rely on case management systems, and legal notices and subscriptions are needed regardless of the economy.

big_ticket.reason: Court case management system implementations are large multi-year projects that are rare for each customer.

people_delivered.reason: Revenue comes mainly from proprietary software and publications, not from staff time. Journalists and implementers support those products.

large_customers.reason: The main software buyers are government courts and agencies. Law firms buy the newspaper.

asset_heavy.reason: Software and publishing need little physical investment beyond offices and some printing.

notes: Journal Technologies (software) is treated as the larger part of the business. The legal newspaper publishing business is smaller.
